title: Package MCP stdio for real client use

context.summary: Turn the MCP stdio server from a runnable app into a documented package that real MCP clients can spawn.
context.background: MCP tools are implemented and acceptance exercises the registry, but the Compose stdio service is mainly a smoke artifact. Real use needs client config examples and a spawn smoke test.

in: Add documented MCP client configuration examples for local API usage.
Add a spawn smoke test that starts apps/mcp/dist/stdio.js as a child process.
Verify the stdio server exposes upload/search/memory/context/job tools through the MCP SDK.
Clarify when MCP should be launched as a process versus represented in Compose.
Update MCP docs and validation scripts.
out: Convert MCP stdio into an HTTP server.
Bypass the HTTP API from MCP.

acceptance_criteria: Docs include copyable MCP client config examples.
A smoke script can spawn the stdio server and initialize/list tools.
Smoke coverage includes at least one tool call through the HTTP API.
MCP package does not import DB, Redis or storage internals.

manual_checks: Confirm MCP client examples use env vars instead of hardcoded secrets.
Confirm Compose docs do not imply stdio is a network daemon.

risks: Stdio smoke tests can hang if process lifecycle handling is incomplete.
Different MCP clients may require slightly different config shapes.
definition_of_done: Task status is changed to accepted or done.
Branch is committed and merged back into master.
